title: LONG-RUNNING TASKS
subtitle: If work takes longer than a request should, accept it, queue it, and let the client check back.
footer: Theory: DDIA ch 11 Stream processing · DDIA ch 8 Trouble with distributed systems

items: Work takes more than a second or two: transcoding, report generation, code execution, model inference.
Work is bursty and expensive, so it needs backpressure.
Doing heavy work inside the request: timeouts, retried requests duplicate work, and no backpressure.
Return a job ID immediately; enqueue the work. Workers scale independently of the API.
Workers update the job status; the client polls or subscribes (SSE/WebSocket) for progress.
Failures retry with backoff (visibility timeout); poison jobs go to a dead-letter queue. Jobs must be idempotent.
Return a job ID immediately (HTTP 202) and enqueue the work.
Workers scale on queue depth, independently of the API.
Store status (queued, running, done, failed); clients poll or subscribe.
Retry with backoff using a visibility timeout; send poison jobs to a dead-letter queue.
Make jobs idempotent: a retried job must not duplicate side effects.

blocks.text: "Submission returns a job ID right away. The job goes on a queue; autoscaled workers run it and update its status, and the client polls every second."

items: Doing heavy work inside the HTTP request.
No dead-letter queue, so one bad job blocks or loops forever.
Non-idempotent jobs combined with at-least-once delivery.
